sources.entry: _A hand-picked collection of the finest of resources for the most awesome of agents, Claude Code, the undisputed champion of coding companions, from the unstoppable team at Anthropic PBC. A delectable showcase of top tier skills, ambidextrous agents, scintillating status lines, top notch developer tooling, and also we have plugins. Suitable for beginners and veterans, with an emphasis on code qual

summary.one_liner: Official home of Claude Code, Anthropic's agentic coding tool that runs in the terminal and works on your codebase through natural language commands.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Claude Code as an agentic coding tool that runs in your terminal, understands your codebase, and handles routine tasks, code explanation, and git workflows via natural language. It says the tool can be used from the terminal, an IDE, or by tagging @claude on GitHub. Install options listed are a curl script (macOS/Linux), Homebrew cask, a PowerShell command (Windows), and WinGet; npm install is marked deprecated. The README points to official documentation for setup, uninstall, and troubleshooting. It also covers plugins (developed in a separate claude-plugins-official repo), bug reporting via the /bug command or GitHub issues, a Discord community, and data collection and privacy practices. The README does not describe internal architecture or code in this repository.
use_cases: Run an AI coding assistant in the terminal on a project
Execute routine coding tasks with natural language
Explain complex code in an existing codebase
Automate git workflows through an agent
Use an AI coding agent from an IDE or GitHub mentions
Report bugs in an AI coding tool
notable: Terminal-first agentic coding assistant that works across a project's codebase
Can be used from the terminal, an IDE, or by tagging @claude on GitHub
Built-in /bug command for reporting issues from within the tool
Plugins are maintained in a separate official plugins repository
caveats: npm installation is deprecated in favor of the native installers
README is short and defers setup, uninstall, and troubleshooting to external documentation
Collects usage data, conversation data, and /bug feedback; governed by external commercial terms and privacy policy
keywords: run ai in my project folder
